recipes.name: Kielbasa with Brussels Sprouts
ingredients_raw: 1 (16 ounce) package kielbasa sausage, sliced into 1/2 inch pieces
14 ounces baby Brussels sprouts, trimmed and cut in half
salt and ground black pepper to taste

steps.text: Heat oil in a large skillet over medium-high heat. Add sausage and onion; cook and stir until onion is translucent, 8 to 10 minutes. Add Brussels sprouts; cook 10 minutes more. Season with salt and black pepper.

raw_recipe.headline: Kielbasa with Brussels Sprouts
raw_recipe.description: For this recipe, sliced kielbasa sausage is cooked with Brussels sprouts and red onion to make a fast and hearty main dish with only six ingredients.

review.reviewBody: This is sooooo good--here's a little tip from an old German lady--It's ok to use 2-3 Tbs of water in place of the canola oil for cooking the kielbasa,(kielbasa is already greasy) onions, and brussel sprouts, just keep an eye on it and add more water as it evaporates--the onions will still sweeten up and carmelize cooked in water.

I have a slight variation of this dish, and use it as a main dish. Marinate the brussel sprouts, onions and kielbasa with the seasonings listed, but add chopped garlic and mushrooms. Bake in the oven until the brussel sprouts are to your liking. YUM!

This was a great basic recipe to build upon. I added beer to the pan with the oil and onion and sauteed it with the kielbasa. I added a little more beer with the brussel sprouts, then I covered the pan to let the ingredients simmer in the liquid. When the sprouts were cooked through, I took them and the kielbasa out and put them in a bowl to hold. I then added more oil to the pan and some roasted garlic smashed with salt. I then deglazed the pan with beer, and kept slowly adding more beer to get to the consistency I wanted. I added some dijon mustard and salt and pepper to taste, then added the kielbasa and sprouts back into the pan and tossed to coat. I served it with parmesan and cracked pepper polenta... delicious!

This was sooo good!!! I followed the recipe as listed but also added some suggestions from another reviewer... I cooked the onions and sausage as listed but added beer. I added more beer with the brussel sprouts to deglaze the pan and cooked covered for 10 minutes. I removed the Brussels and sausage then added roasted garlic, beer, a little oil, and a dash of horseradish. I cooked this down until the beer bubbled. Finally, I added the sausage and Brussels and tossed for a few more minutes. It was delicious!! Thanks to the previous reviewer for these great suggestions. Will definitely be adding this to our dinner rotation!!

Took advice of using 2tbsp of water instead of all that oil & 1 tbsp of “can’t believe it’s not butter “. Worked perfectly!. Made both hubby and self happy. He ate lots more kielbasa, I ate almost all the Brussels sprouts. Added 2 largely diced potatoes as another suggested that I cooked in micro for 1 minute before adding to all the other Ingredients. Next time i’m Going to try it with broccoli only because hubby likes that more.

I made this dish using fresh Kielbasa, so I had to disregard the cook times entirely. Started the Kielbasa on the stove top and fried it adequately, before transferring it to the sheet pan of Brussel Sprouts and Red Onion. In the oven, the dish finished well, and was tasty.

I made this but I added garlic and seasond with Mrs Dash chipotl. I sauteed the brussel sprouts garlic and Red onion along with sliced potatoes. Then I added both the keilbasa and garlic chicken sausage. When potatoes were a little crispy and cooked I covered it with shredded cheddar

I do not cook with a lot of grease, so I omitted the Canola oil and sautéed the sausage and opinion it the fat from the sausage. I also pre seasoned the sprouts with seasoned salt and a touch of olive oil.
This is great! I added some veggie broth at the end to deglaze the pan and just give it some moisture. It's a keeper.

This was absolutely delicious. My mom and I cooked it together and she added maple syrup and bourbon to the dish. We steamed the brussel sprouts for 8 minutes before putting them in with the kielbasa, onions and mushrooms which we added. Probably one of the best dishes I've had in a long time. We served it with garlic mashed potatoes, french bread, and Pinot Noir.

This was very easy to prepare however it needs a bit more flavor. Next time I would cook the brussel sprouts first then add the kielbasa and onion. I cooked it twice as long as recommended and the brussel sprouts were still firm.
I always roast my Brussels sprouts, but after making them this way, I'm sold! The combination of flavors is tremendous. And did I mention how easy it is to make? Kids loved it.
Easy one skillet meal and I had a side of baked beans with it. Delish!
This is a staple in my home! love it with egg noodles and honey mustard on the side, YUM! Cooked as the recipient states.
Delightfully simple to make. Needed something like a sauce, so the 2nd time I made it I added some hot sauce, jalapeno peppers and some cheese. Great improvement.

The recipe was great. I felt like I needed to add chicken stock but I usually stick with the original recipe however I did add garlic powder and no salt. Tasty....when I make it again, I am going to add 1/2 cup of low sodium chicken broth.
Even brussels sprout haters will love this savory dish!

I sliced up my Brussels and sauteed with chopped sweet onions. I also added a couple tablespoons of apple cider vinegar for brininess. I added turkey Kielbasa,which is less greasy, but you can slice Italian, bratwurst, or veggie sausages. Had a small corn muffin with it. So delicious!

This turned out great! My husband and son loved it and said it now the go to recipe for kielbasa. The addition of potato cooked in butter in a skillet made a great side dish and the German mustard was a nice addition as a condiment, if needed.

We enjoyed this recipe, being fans of kielbasa, Brussels sprouts and onion. The recipe calls for baby Brussels sprouts, but they are a bit hard to come by. I had larger ones and should have cut them smaller to ensure they would cook to the right tenderness. They were a bit too hard for my taste. If I had cooked longer, the onion would have scorched. I would like to be able to give this 4.5 stars instead of 5.
